# Generated files and ownership

Ghost treats its Markdown as a view over canonical state, not as the source of
truth. That split decides who may edit what and when Ghost may overwrite a file.

## Ownership classes

| Class | Files | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical state | `.ghost/state.json`, `.ghost/project.json`, `.ghost/config.toml` | Written atomically by Ghost. Existing `state.json` is never replaced by `new`, `init`, or `regen`. |
| User-editable source | `.ghost/answers.json` | Read and rewritten by Ghost. Edit it, then run `ghost regen --force` when rendered files conflict. |
| Generated views | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `STATE.md`, `specs/00-overview.md`, `specs/feature-<slug>.md`, `scripts/check.sh`, `scripts/dev.sh`, `.opencode/commands/*.md`, `.claude/commands/*.md`, `opencode.json` | Ghost owns the initial content. Local edits are detected through the manifest. |
| User-owned scaffold | `specs/schema.yaml` | Created once as a TODO scaffold; later edits are treated like any generated view for overwrite purposes. |
| Append-only metadata | `.gitignore` | Ghost appends five entries without duplicating or removing existing lines. |
| Task records | `.ghost/tasks/<id>.json` | Written atomically by `ghost task`; never rendered or overwritten by `new`/`init`/`regen`. |
| Journal | `.ghost/events.jsonl` | Append-only, metadata-only. Ghost never rewrites past lines. |
| Handoff snapshot | `.ghost/handoff.json` | Replaced atomically by each `ghost handoff`. |
| Verification evidence | `.ghost/evidence/<run-id>.json` | Written atomically by `ghost verify`; never overwritten. |
| Verify allowlist | `.ghost/verify.json` | Optional and user-owned; Ghost reads it and never writes it. |

## Adapter surfaces

| Adapter | Instructions | Project commands | Model config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenCode | `AGENTS.md` | `.opencode/commands/*.md` | `opencode.json` when a model override is set |
| Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` | `.claude/commands/*.md` | none |
| Codex | `AGENTS.md` | none (not a supported project surface) | none |

Shared views (`STATE.md`, specs, scripts) are emitted once for any combination of
adapters. `AGENTS.md` is written when OpenCode or Codex is selected; `CLAUDE.md`
only when Claude Code is selected. Command files carry adapter-specific
frontmatter: OpenCode may select a known agent and model, Claude uses
`argument-hint`, and Codex receives no command files.

Changing the adapter selection does not delete a previous adapter's directory
(`.opencode/` or `.claude/`). Those files may contain local edits, so removing
them remains a manual decision; see the deletion policy below.

`STATE.md` is the human-readable view of `.ghost/state.json`. `ghost status`
prefers canonical state. Handoff commands still edit `STATE.md` in the v1
surface; the migration path imports its sections into `state.json`.

## Manifest and conflict detection

After every successful `new`, `init`, or `regen`, Ghost writes
`.ghost/generated-manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "generated_at": "2026-11-19T12:00:00+05:30",
  "files": {
    "AGENTS.md": "<sha256>",
    "STATE.md": "<sha256>"
  }
}
```

On the next run, each target falls into one of these cases:

| Current file | Manifest entry | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missing | any | Write |
| Matches the new content | none (v1 project) | Adopt silently; no data loss |
| Matches the recorded hash | present | Write |
| Differs from the recorded hash | present | Conflict: `modified since generation` |
| Differs from the new content | none | Conflict: `not generated by ghost` |
| Symlink | any | Conflict, and `--force` cannot bypass it |

`new` keeps the v1 rule: any existing generated target is refused without
`--force`. `init` and `regen` allow idempotent re-runs when hashes and content
match, but refuse real conflicts.

Conflict output names every path and tells the user to pass `--force`. `--force`
replaces conflicting regular files. It never replaces a symlink and never
permits a path outside the project root.

## Safe write protocol

Every generated file is written by `src/persist.rs`:

1. Validate the relative path: no absolute path, `.`, or `..`.
2. Walk existing components and refuse symlinks.
3. Create parent directories.
4. Write a unique temporary sibling.
5. `fsync` the temporary file.
6. Set the executable bit when needed.
7. Atomically rename over the target.
8. `fsync` the parent directory.

A `.ghost/.lock` file serializes Ghost commands. A lock owned by a dead process is
reclaimed; a live owner causes a clear error instead of concurrent writes.

## v1 to v2 migration

| v1 artifact | v2 action |
| --- | --- |
| `.ghost/answers.json` | Read as before; `deadline` is now optional for normal profiles |
| `STATE.md` | Imported into `.ghost/state.json` before the view is replaced |
| Generated files without a manifest | Adopted when content matches; otherwise conflict |
| `.gitignore` entries | Preserved and not duplicated |
| `opencode.json` | Treated as generated only when `model_override` is set |

Migration never requires re-interviewing. `ghost init --force` on an existing v1
project imports the handoff view and refreshes the views in one step.

## Deletion policy

Ghost does not delete files. Removing a feature from `answers.json` and running
`regen` leaves its old `specs/feature-<slug>.md` in place. This is deliberate:
the file may contain user-written scenarios. Delete it manually after reviewing
the diff.
